answer: One workable design: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because nadir only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, umber is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any mesa approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
